title.en: A bet and an invisible chair

text.en: Mario loved to say that he had lots of friends. His grandfather bet him a fruit chaat that many of them were not real friends. To prove it, the grandfather gave him a chair nobody could see. Let us find out what happened when Mario tried to sit on it.

Friendship has many words: partner, buddies, companion, classmates and friend. The book asks you to complete these words and to find words like helpful, loyal, loving, laughter and hope in a grid. Think of what you call a friend in your own language, because the idea of friendship exists in every language.
Mario loves having many friends. He shows off a lot, always boasting about how many friends he has and how friendly he is with everyone. One day his grandfather says that he bets a fruit chaat that Mario does not have as many friends as he thinks. Many of them are only companions or partners. Mario accepts the bet readily, but does not know how to test who his real friends are. So he asks his grandfather for help.
The grandfather goes to the attic, which is a storage space just under the roof, and returns holding something Mario cannot see. He says it is a very special chair. Since it is invisible, it is tricky to sit on. If Mario takes it to school and manages to sit on it, the magic will work and he will know who his real friends are. The chair is invisible and special. The test is not about the chair at all but about how the friends behave.
Brave and determined, Mario takes the invisible chair to school. At break time he asks everyone to form a circle and says they are about to see something amazing. He tries to sit on the chair, misses and falls on his backside. His classmates laugh a lot. He says there is just a technical problem, tries again and falls again. Still he does not give up, which shows he is strong-willed. At last he does not fall. He is sitting in mid-air, because three buddies, Guneet, Asma and Deepa, are holding him up.
Looking around, Mario sees that many he thought of as friends only made fun of him and enjoyed each fall. He leaves with his three real friends and explains how his grandfather cleverly found a way to show that true friends are those who care for us. A real friend does not enjoy your bad luck, but helps you when you fall.
That evening the four children go to Mario's grandfather, as Mario has won the bet. They have a great time listening to stories and eating lots of fruit chaat. From then on, they used the magic chair test on many occasions. Whoever passed became a friend for life. The lesson is that true friends are measured by how they treat us in difficult moments, not by how many we count.
A root word is the main word, and a suffix is a group of letters added after it. In friendly the root is friend and the suffix is ly. Suddenly has root sudden and suffix ly. Examples: magic plus al gives magical, care plus ful gives careful, celebrate plus tion gives celebration, laugh plus ing gives laughing, wonder plus ful gives wonderful, help plus ful gives helpful, friend plus ship gives friendship, courage plus ous gives courageous. Notice spelling changes: celebrate loses its e before tion becomes celebration.
Words that describe a person or thing are adjectives. The chair was invisible and special. Mario was brave and determined. Match adjectives to nouns, such as brave soldier, clever plan, tasty peanuts, heavy rain, slight cold and true friends. A sentence: The brave soldier marched ahead. Describing a person with adjectives is a good skill for stories and messages.
In pairs, choose four qualities you want in a friend, such as honest, loyal, kind or caring, and give reasons using: I feel my friend should be, because. Other qualities include loving, respectful, polite, team-worker and understanding. Mario wrote thank-you messages to Deepa, Guneet and Asma. In them he says he feels special and blessed, and that he can always depend on them. Write your own message to your best friend, borrowing ideas from The Unlikely Best Friends and A Friend's Prayer. An acrostic poem uses each letter of the word FRIENDS to begin a line describing friends.

board.text: Speaking and writing: letters to friends

text.en: Mario wrote thank-you messages to Deepa, Guneet and Asma. In them he says he feels special and blessed, and that he can always depend on them.
Write your own message to your best friend, borrowing ideas from The Unlikely Best Friends and A Friend's Prayer.
An acrostic poem uses each letter of the word FRIENDS to begin a line describing friends.

problem.en: Split into root and suffix: friendly, suddenly, helpful.

text.en: Find the main word that carries the meaning.

why.en: The root word is the base of the word.

text.en: Friendly is friend plus ly. Suddenly is sudden plus ly. Helpful is help plus ful.

problem.en: Match adjectives with nouns to make phrases: brave, clever, tasty, heavy, true.

text.en: Ask which noun fits the feeling or quality.

why.en: An adjective must make sense with the noun.

text.en: Brave soldier, clever plan, tasty peanuts, heavy rain, true friends.

why.en: More than one pair is possible, such as heavy cold, so check meaning.

prompt.en: Explain how the magic chair test showed Mario who his real friends were.

requiredIdeas.en: The chair was invisible and tricky to sit on.
Real friends care and help when we fall.

commonMisconceptions.en: The laughing friends were real friends.

points.en: The Chair is a story about Mario and an invisible chair.
His grandfather bet a fruit chaat that Mario did not have so many real friends.
Guneet, Asma and Deepa held him up; the others laughed.
True friends care for us in difficult moments.
Root words and suffixes build words such as friendly and helpful.
Adjectives describe nouns, such as brave soldier and true friends.
